Changed from toggle to select inputType to resolve issues:
- Toggle was outputting "True" instead of the masking instruction text
- Label now correctly shows as "Masked Image" instead of "Option 1"

New implementation uses select dropdown with:
- Option 1 (default): Empty string for full image editing
- Option 2: Complete masking instruction text

This provides the intended functionality of conditionally appending masking instructions to the prompt.

body:
### Summary
<!--- General summary / title -->
Add multi-endpoint cache connection pool support

### Description

<!--- Details of what you changed -->
Enables the driver to support multiple cache cluster endpoints with independent connection pools, allowing different database connections to use different cache clusters.

Refactored CacheConnection to support multiple cache endpoints by implementing a per-endpoint connection pool registry:

#### Key Changes
1. Per-Endpoint Pool Registry: 

- Added `static ConcurrentHashMap<String, GenericObjectPool>` registry to store pools per unique endpoint
- Pool keys use format `"RW:<endpoint>" or "RO:<endpoint>"` to prevent collisions when same endpoint is used for both read and write
- Pools are shared across `CacheConnection` instances with identical endpoints

2. Pool Lifecycle Management: 

- Changed from static pools to instance-level volatile fields that reference shared pools from registry
- Implemented thread-safe pool creation using double-checked locking with separate READ_LOCK and WRITE_LOCK
- Pool size can only increase (never decrease) when reused by connections with larger pool size requirements

body:
## Summary

Fixed a critical issue in `amp.sh` where additional command-line arguments were not being forwarded to the Claude CLI. This was breaking session resume functionality and potentially other CLI features that rely on additional arguments.

## Changes

- **amp.sh**: Added `"$@"` to properly pass all command-line arguments through to Claude Code
  - Restores session resume functionality (e.g., `amp --resume <session-id>`)
  - Fixes any other CLI flags that weren't being forwarded
  - Simple one-character fix with significant impact

- **reload-amp.sh**: Enhanced development workflow with cache management
  - Now clears Claude Code shell snapshot cache to ensure updated scripts are used
  - Added `--keep-cache` flag for selective cache clearing
  - Improved argument parsing to support multiple flags
  - Better user feedback when running in active Claude sessions
  - Enhanced help messages and documentation

## Problem Solved

When users tried to resume Claude Code sessions using `amp --resume <session-id>` or pass other CLI flags, the arguments were silently dropped. The `amp.sh` script was only passing the workspace system prompt and directory to Claude, ignoring all additional arguments. This completely broke session resume and any other features requiring additional CLI flags.

The `reload-amp.sh` improvements address a related development workflow issue where updated scripts weren't being picked up by active Claude sessions due to shell snapshot caching.

## Testing

- [x] Tested session resume: `amp --resume <session-id>` now works correctly
- [x] Tested normal amp launch: `amp` still works without additional arguments
- [x] Verified reload-amp.sh clears snapshot cache properly
- [x] Tested --keep-cache flag works as expected
- [x] Documentation reviewed for accuracy
- [x] CHANGELOG.md updated with user-facing descriptions

## Related

Addresses user reports of session resume not working and development workflow friction when updating amp.sh scripts.

author: jpagh
body:
This PR is to fix the issues brought up in the Slack thread that is screenshotted below.

The root of the issue is that when you're in a `force_ask` event due to the review screen edit, you can't edit the list items, "Input not processed". The workaround I did here is to gather the lists as empty from the interview flow if the items aren't needed. Then if they edit, the `revisit` screens are shown where the user can add and edit items, rather than going back through the "interview" flow and trying to `gather()` again.

There are some caveats with these changes:

- The user loses the yes/no radio buttons on edits. I cannot come up with an alternative that works and retains them, since there's no way to use the `yesnoradio` with the `add_action` that is required on the `revisit` screen.
- I made it so that if the user gets onto the debt list page, they have to enter at least one debt (if they get there through the interview flow they'll have had to enter one debt already, if they get there via the edit flow they'll have to enter one or they'll get a validation error saying so).
- It is possible to say that you have personal property that needs to be handled and then skip adding any (this was possible before as well).
- I put all of the questions onto one page for each of the sections so that I could handle the "need_items" determinations with validation code because I could not get `depends on` or `on change` to work consistently.
- I clear the list if the user edits their answer to the section questions in a way that would cause them to not need to provide those items. This is different than before where I would just leave the list un-gathered. This is probably safer in terms of the documents not triggering list gathering, but potentially worse if the user adds a bunch of items, edits the question clearing the list, and then later decides that they did actually have items they wanted, since they will have to re-enter those items.

I also re-arranged `vehicles` in the review screen to match the interview flow.

author: copilot
body:
The permissions step was creating the business user entity (DDL) instead of only applying grants; schema creation must happen earlier and separately.

- **Schema step added**: Introduced `ensureDatabaseEntities` and `db:schema` script to create business tables before grants; integrated into full provisioning with a short delay between stages.
- **Permissions scoped**: Permissions now only create the base role and apply grants; log messages aligned to English.
- **Docs & scripts**: README and db-architecture updated to reflect the new setup order and commands.

Example:

```bash
npm run db:setup   # create DB/user
npm run db:schema  # create entities (e.g., users table)
npm run db:permissions  # apply base role and grants
npm run db:seed    # smoke test as app user
```

author: shadymccoy
body:
Add four concrete Corp implementations following the economic model:
- SpawningCorp: sells work-ticks, carry-ticks, move-ticks; buys energy
- MiningCorp: buys work-ticks, sells energy at source location
- HaulingCorp: buys energy at source, sells at destination (arbitrage)
- UpgradingCorp: buys energy + work-ticks, sells rcl-progress (triggers mint)

Add Node module for territory management:
- Node interface with territory positions and resources
- NodeSurveyor for identifying resources and potential corps
- Pure functions for node operations (pruning, offers, balance)

Add Colony orchestrator:
- Manages nodes, corps, and chains
- Runs economic cycle: survey, collect offers, fund chains, settle payments
- Handles credit minting for achievements and taxation
- Supports serialization for persistence

All Corp types include:
- Cost-plus pricing with wealth-based margin (5-10%)
- Input/output offer generation
- Performance statistics tracking
- Pure functions for testing calculations

Comprehensive unit tests for all new components (465 tests pass).

Changes:
- Add set_seed() function that sets seeds for random, numpy, torch
- Add SEED=42 constant to frozen configuration
- Enable torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic for reproducibility
- Log seed value at startup
- Include seed in summary_report.json for traceability

This ensures reproducible results across runs, which is essential for valid walk-forward validation comparisons.

body:
Created a new function that generates a frame-by-frame CSV from vstim_go with all fixation detection and target metrics for troubleshooting.

Output CSV includes ALL frames (not just fixation points) with:
- frame_to_frame_movement: Velocity at each frame
- trial_number: Which trial the frame belongs to
- target info: target_x, target_y, target_diameter, target_visible
- distance_from_target: Distance from eye to target center
- contact_threshold: target_radius + cursor_radius
- within_contact_threshold: Boolean flag for cursor touching target
- in_fixation: Boolean flag - is this frame part of a detected fixation?
- fixation_id: Which fixation within the trial (if in_fixation=True)
- point_index_in_fixation: Position within the fixation
- time_since_fixation_start: Time elapsed since fixation began

This CSV makes it easy to:
1. See which frames are/aren't detected as fixations
2. Verify contact threshold calculations
3. Debug why fixations might be missed
4. Analyze temporal dynamics of fixation detection

  df = create_vstim_go_fixation_csv(

author: abhiek187
body: _The server implementation of #373_ 3 OAuth endpoints have been created: 1. **GET /oauth** - Gets all the URLs from each OAuth provider to perform an authorization code flow. This is intended to be called on the sign-in page to present all the available sign-in options. I was able to integrate Facebook, GitHub, and Google. I went to their respective dev portals to register an app and obtain the client credentials to sign in on the server side. I wasn't able to get Microsoft working due to limitations in linking the tokens to Firebase. Yahoo may have similar issues. And Apple requires a developer membership. The downside is that Firebase may not return the most up-to-date or secure auth endpoint for each provider. We would need to modify each endpoint manually to add these parameters. 2. **POST /oauth** - This is the most complex endpoint, and it's split into 2 parts. (Maybe I should create a diagram that visualizes this process.) a. If the chef isn't signed in, this signs them in using the chosen OAuth provider. Before calling this endpoint, the client must open the auth URL in an embedded WebView to complete the sign-in process for the IdP (identity provider). They will be redirected back to the app with a code that must be passed to this endpoint. (Side note: I will need to create a custom URL scheme/App Link for the mobile apps so they can be redirected properly. Let's see if iOS will allow the capability without a membership.) The code is exchanged for an ID or access token specific to a platform. Even though we're not redirecting back to the client, the redirect URL must match the previous request. This involved looking up the right token endpoint for each provider and handling all the different responses. Finally, this token can be exchanged for a Firebase token, which gives all the necessary credentials to create/update the chef in MongoDB and sign them in. An account is created if the email isn't linked to an existing account. If the account already exists with that provider, the chef is signed in. We can determine this by checking if the UID exists in MongoDB. However, if the email is already associated with a different account (through a different provider or the normal password route), Firebase will return a FEDERATED_USER_ID_ALREADY_LINKED or EMAIL_EXISTS error. To respect email enumeration protection, we don't tell the chef that this email was already linked to a different provider. Just present a generic error instead. For this to work, the user must sign in using their original provider and then link the other provider in their settings. This also means we're not allowed to filter specific sign-in methods that the chef is allowed to use. Another possible error is if the email being linked isn't verified yet. We can either error out or redirect the chef to verify their email. I'll have to see how common this is in practice. b. If the chef is signed in, this links an OAuth provider to their account. On the backend, the main change is that we pass the Firebase token when we exchange the OAuth token. This will allow any OAuth provider to be linked to the existing account, even if the emails differ. But if that account is already linked to a different account, we still return the FEDERATED_USER_ID_ALREADY_LINKED error. We don't need to persist the provider data in MongoDB; that will be handled by calling Firebase. If the chef wants to link a regular password, they can leverage the existing Change Password functionality. 4. **DELETE /oauth** - Unlinks an OAuth provider from the chef's account. The chef must be signed in, and this option can be made available in their profile settings. The API itself doesn't make it obvious if the operation was successful, but we can call GET /chef to check if the provider was removed. Speaking of which, this PR also enhances that endpoint to include all the linked providers. So yeah...OAuth! I'm just redacting the client secret in the logs, but I don't think I need to do the same for the tokens since those are all temporary. (And for the auth codes in particular, they will be invalidated after one use, even on failure.)

body:
# Description

This change is correlated with DUNE-DAQ/integrationtest#138.

In recent discussions about improvements that people would like to see in the available regression tests, it was mentioned that it would be helpful if the log files, etc. from failed tests did not disappear as quickly as they sometimes do.

We looked into options that are available with pytest, but it didn't seem possible to save directories from failed tests longer than ones from successful tests.

So, we have added logic to our "bundle" scripts to do this.  (initially, just the `daqsystemtest` bundle script)

The complication with doing that, is that it is not obvious how to get a run of the pytest program to return the name of the current pytest subdirectory (e.g. `/tmp/pytest-of-${USER}/pytest-1234`).  

One idea was to have the `integrationtest` infrastructure code print the pytest output directory name to the console, capture that in the bundle script, etc.  Unfortunately, that wouldn't work when we have the `--concise-output` option enabled in the bundle script (the purpose of that option is to _suppress_ the console output).

The idea that I implemented was to have the bundle script pass some unique keys to the `integrationtest` infrastructure, have the `integrationtest` infrastructure write that information to a file in the pytest output directory, and have the bundle script look for a file with the relevant keys to find which pytest subdir corresponds to the most recent test.  

Once the bundle script knows the correct pytest output directory, it is easy to make a copy of it.  

The bundle script also now has logic to clean up old "failed" pytest output dirs (older than 26 hours or more than 10 failed directories).

Here are suggested steps for testing these changes.   These steps locally modified the `readout_type_scan_test` so that it often/always fails, and with that, we can see the creation of "failed" pytest output directories happening.

```
DATE_PREFIX=`date '+%d%b'`
TIME_SUFFIX=`date '+%H%M'`

source /cvmfs/dunedaq.opensciencegrid.org/setup_dunedaq.sh
setup_dbt latest
dbt-create -n NFD_DEV_251216_A9 ${DATE_PREFIX}FDDevTest_${TIME_SUFFIX}
cd ${DATE_PREFIX}FDDevTest_${TIME_SUFFIX}/sourcecode

git clone https://github.com/DUNE-DAQ/daqsystemtest.git -b kbiery/copy_failed_integtest_dirs
cd ..

dbt-workarea-env

git clone https://github.com/DUNE-DAQ/integrationtest.git -b kbiery/copy_failed_integtest_dirs
cd integrationtest; pip install -U . ; cd ..

dbt-build -j 12
dbt-workarea-env

sed -i 's,"min_size_bytes": 7272,"min_size_bytes": 7273,' sourcecode/daqsystemtest/integtest/readout_type_scan_test.py

daqsystemtest_integtest_bundle.sh -k readout_type_scan --stop-on-fail --concise-output
echo ""
echo -e "\U1F535 \U2705 Note that when the regression test failed, a copy of the pytest output directory was created. \U2705 \U1F535"
```

## Type of change

- [x] New feature or enhancement (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## Testing checklist

- [x] Minimal system quicktest passes (`pytest -s minimal_system_quick_test.py`)
- [x] Full set of integration tests pass (`daqsystemtest_integtest_bundle.sh`)

## Further checks

- [x] Code is commented where needed, particularly in hard-to-understand areas

body:
## Summary
- Fixes "invalid ISO 8601 string: Sun Dec 14" error on ticketing screen when opening time entry dialog

## Root Cause
Migration `20251214120000_time_entry_work_date.cjs` changed `time_periods.start_date` and `end_date` from `timestamp` to `date` type. The PostgreSQL `pg` driver returns JavaScript `Date` objects for DATE columns, but the code was treating them as strings.

**Error flow:**
1. Database returns DATE as JS `Date` object
2. `TimePeriod.findByDate()` passed it through as-is
3. `getCurrentTimePeriod()` called `.toString()` → `"Sun Dec 14 2024 00:00:00 GMT..."`
4. `TimeEntryDialog` called `.slice(0, 10)` → `"Sun Dec 14"`
5. `Temporal.PlainDate.from("Sun Dec 14")` threw the error

## Changes
- Update `DbTimePeriod` interface to reflect `string | Date` for date fields
- Update `fromDbDate()` to handle both strings and Date objects
- Update `findByDate()` to convert Date objects to ISO strings

## Test plan
- [ ] Open a ticket in the ticketing dashboard
- [ ] Click the timer/add time entry button
- [ ] Verify the time entry dialog opens without error

author: abhipatel12
body:
## Summary

This PR adds support for friendly names and descriptions in hook configurations, aligning the implementation with the official documentation. It fixes a bug where hooks disabled by name in settings were being ignored because the system only recognized command paths as identifiers.

## Details

- **Naming Support**: Hooks now support optional `name` and `description` fields in `settings.json` and extension `hooks.json`.
- **Identification**: `HookRegistry` now prefers the user-defined `name` for identification and disabling logic, with a fallback to the `command` string for backward compatibility.
- **Enhanced Deduplication**: Improved `HookPlanner` to deduplicate hooks based on the combination of `name` and `command`, preventing accidental shadowing of distinct hooks sharing a script.
- **UI Improvements**: Updated the `/hooks panel` and tab-completion to display friendly names as primary identifiers and included descriptions for better context.
- **Documentation**: Updated `docs/hooks/index.md` and regenerated the settings schema to accurately describe the new behavior, execution order, and persistent storage.

## Related Issues

Resolves issue #15063.

## How to Validate

1. **Verify Friendly Names**:
   - Add a hook with a `name` property to your `.gemini/settings.json`.
   - Run `/hooks panel` and verify that the friendly name is displayed as the title.
   - Run `/hooks disable <name>` and verify the hook is disabled and recorded in `~/.gemini/settings.json`.

2. **Verify Backward Compatibility**:
   - Add a hook without a `name` property.
   - Verify it still appears in `/hooks panel` (using the command path).
   - Verify it can still be disabled using its command string.

3. **Verify Deduplication**:
   - Add two hooks with the same command but different names.
   - Verify both appear and execute independently.

4. **Run Unit Tests**:
   ```bash
   npx vitest packages/core/src/hooks/hookRegistry.test.ts packages/core/src/hooks/hookPlanner.test.ts packages/cli/src/ui/commands/hooksCommand.test.ts
   ```

- [x] Noted breaking changes (if any)

  - Added CI validation step in `server-tox.yml` workflow

body:
## Summary

Add 11 new fuzzers targeting the raw libjpeg API to complement existing TurboJPEG API fuzzers. These target code paths not covered by the TurboJPEG wrapper layer, achieving ~95% coverage of security-critical API surface.

## New Fuzzers

| Fuzzer | Target APIs | Security Focus |
|--------|-------------|----------------|
| `decompress_libjpeg` | `jpeg_read_header`, `jpeg_read_scanlines` | Slow-path Huffman, colorspaces, scaling |
| `progressive` | `jpeg_start_output`, `jpeg_consume_input` | Buffered-image state machine |
| `marker` | `jpeg_save_markers`, `jpeg_set_marker_processor` | Custom markers, ICC multi-chunk |
| `coefficient` | `jpeg_read_coefficients` | DCT coefficient memory access |
| `partial` | `jpeg_skip_scanlines`, `jpeg_crop_scanline` | Partial decode bounds |
| `error_recovery` | `jpeg_abort`, `jpeg_abort_decompress` | Cleanup paths, object reuse |
| `raw_data` | `jpeg_read_raw_data` | Raw YUV plane access |
| `transcode` | `jpeg_read_coefficients`, `jpeg_write_coefficients` | Lossless transcoding |
| `compress_libjpeg` | `jpeg_write_scanlines`, `jpeg_write_marker` | Compression buffers |
| `compress_raw_data` | `jpeg_write_raw_data` | Raw YUV compression |
| `resync` | `jpeg_resync_to_restart` | Restart marker recovery |

## Also Included

- **jpeg.dict**: Comprehensive JPEG dictionary (150+ entries) for libFuzzer
- **fuzzer.options**: Timeout and memory limit configuration
- **Seed corpora**: 12 specialized corpus zip files for different fuzzer types
- **Updated build.sh**: Distributes dictionaries and corpora to all fuzzers

## Testing

- All 21 fuzzers build successfully with Clang + ASan + libFuzzer
- Smoke tested with 100 iterations each
- Compatible with OSS-Fuzz build environment

## Test Plan

- [x] Build with `-DWITH_FUZZ=1` succeeds
- [x] All fuzzers execute without immediate crashes
- [x] Dictionaries and corpora are properly distributed
- [x] ASan/MSan/UBSan builds work correctly

Refines governance skills to be compatible with Stagecraft, implementing warning modes and clean fallbacks.

## Changes
- **Header Comments**: Strictly enforces 'Package' comment by default, supports warned mode via Env Var.
- **Provider Governance**: Removes noisy fallbacks, correctly identifies content gaps.
- **Orphan Docs**: Excludes hidden directories and generated docs.
- **Purity**: Expands allowlist.

Cortex MCP Router Implementation Outline
Executive Summary
This outline defines the steps to implement the Cortex MCP router using Strategy A (Workspace Conversion). cortex/rust will be converted into a Cargo workspace containing xray (existing) and mcp (new). This approach ensures a clean, scalable foundation for future Rust tooling while maintaining backward compatibility for XRAY builds via -p xray. The implementation prioritizes deterministic "self-healing" resolution and a standard stdio transport.

Refinements:

API Surface: Expose resolve_mcp, mount_alias, list_mounts, describe_skills, get_capabilities.
Configurable Roots: Support CORTEX_WORKSPACE_ROOTS env var, default to ~/Dev, ~/src.
Logging: All logs to stderr.
User Review Required
IMPORTANT

Workspace Conversion: The cortex/rust directory will become a Cargo workspace.

Build Impact: cargo build in cortex/rust will now build both xray and cortex-mcp.
Compatibility: CI/Scripts expecting to build only XRAY should use cargo build -p xray. Existing scripts executing inside cortex/rust/xray will continue to work unchanged.
Milestones
1. Workspace Conversion & Crate Scaffolding
Goal: Establish the workspace and new crate structure. Files:

cortex/rust/Cargo.toml
 [NEW]: Workspace manifest.
cortex/rust/mcp/Cargo.toml
 [NEW]: cortex-mcp crate manifest.
cortex/rust/mcp/src/main.rs
 [NEW]: Binary entry point.
cortex/rust/mcp/src/lib.rs
 [NEW]: Library exports.
Changes:

Create Workspace Manifest at 
cortex/rust/Cargo.toml
:
[workspace]
members = ["xray", "mcp"]
resolver = "2"
Create cortex-mcp Manifest at 
cortex/rust/mcp/Cargo.toml
:
name: cortex-mcp
dependencies: rmcp, tokio (full), serde, serde_json, anyhow, thiserror, 
url
, dirs, walkdir.
features:
default = ["transport-stdio", "resolver-local", "skills-core"]
transport-stdio = []
resolver-local = []
skills-core = []
deny-exec = []
Done when: cargo build in cortex/rust successfully builds xray and a stubbed cortex-mcp.

2. Module & Protocol Skeleton
Goal: Create the internal module structure. Files:

src/protocol/mod.rs
, 
src/protocol/types.rs
src/router/mod.rs
src/resolver/mod.rs
src/skills/mod.rs
src/io/mod.rs
src/config/mod.rs
src/util/mod.rs
Changes:

Create mod.rs files to expose the modules.
Implement basic protocol::types for Request/Response if generic rmcp types need extension (likely just re-exports for now).
Done when: cortex-mcp compiles with the full module tree exposed.

3. Filesystem Abstraction (for Testing)
Goal: Enable diskless, deterministic testing. Files:

src/io/fs.rs
: 
RealFs
 implementation (using std::fs).
src/io/memfs.rs
: 
MemFs
 implementation (using HashMap).
Changes:

Define trait Fs: 
read_to_string
, 
read_dir
, 
canonicalize
, 
exists
.
Implement 
RealFs
 calling standard lib.
Implement 
MemFs
 for tests, supporting "mounted" faux contents.
Done when: Unit tests can read/write to 
MemFs
.

4. Deterministic Resolver Implementation
Goal: Implement the core resolution logic. Files:

src/resolver/order.rs
: The resolution pipeline.
src/resolver/alias_map.rs
: .cortex/mcp-aliases.json logic.
src/resolver/workspace.rs
: Workspace scanning.
src/resolver/git_remote.rs
: 
.git/config
 parsing.
Logic:

Candidate Discovery: Scan workspace roots. Filter for directories that are git repos OR have explicit aliases.
Ranking:
Match Rank: 0=Alias, 1=GitRemote, 2=FolderName.
Tie-breaking: Path Depth (asc), Path Lex (asc).
Resolution: Use 
alias_map
 -> git_remote -> 
folder_name
.
Collision: Sort candidates stably. Return match or failure with fix_hint.
Done when: Unit tests resolver_order_is_stable and git_remote_match_beats_name_match pass using 
MemFs
.

5. Transport & Entry Point
Goal: Wire up stdio and the main loop. Files:

src/main.rs
: Parse args, setup logging (stderr), start stdio transport.
src/router/mod.rs
: Handle incoming params, dispatch to resolver.
Changes:

Use rmcp to listen on stdin/stdout.
Register router as the request handler.
Done when: Running cortex-mcp waits for input and responds to initialization.

Integration Plan
Cursor: Configure as an MCP server command: .../cortex/rust/target/release/cortex-mcp.
Antigravity: Call resolve_mcp(name) tool. If successful, use the returned ID to mount the filesystem.
GitHub Actions: Ensure steps use cargo build --workspace or -p flags as needed.
Testing Plan
Fixtures: cortex/rust/mcp/testdata/workspaces_fixture.md (or similar) to describe layout, but primarily use 
MemFs
 in code.
Unit Tests:
test_resolver_priority: Verify Alias > Git > Name.
test_collision_stability: Verify identical inputs produce identical sorted candidate lists.
Future Refactoring: RMCP 0.11.0 Migration
To migrate from the hand-rolled JSON-RPC implementation to rmcp 0.11.0+, follow these specific steps to avoid trait bound and version mismatch issues.

1. Dependency Management
Critical: Do not include schemars as a direct dependency if rmcp exports it. This avoids type mismatches between your schemars::JsonSchema and rmcp's expected trait.

[dependencies]
# Use the re-export from rmcp, or ensure exact version match
rmcp = { version = "0.11.0", features = ["server", "transport-io"] }
serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }
# Remove: schemars = "..."
2. Code Structure
Follow the #[tool_router] pattern strictly. The macro expects specific struct fields and initialization.

use rmcp::{tool_router, tool, ToolRouter};
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct App {
    // Required field for the macro to inject routing logic
    tool_router: ToolRouter<Self>,
    // Your custom fields
    resolver: Arc<ResolveEngine<RealFs>>,
}
// 1. Constructor Block
impl App {
    pub fn new(resolver: ResolveEngine<RealFs>) -> Self {
        Self {
            resolver: Arc::new(resolver),
            // Initialize the router using the generated helper
            tool_router: Self::tool_router(),
        }
    }
}
// 2. Tool Implementation Block
#[tool_router]
impl App {
    #[tool(description = "...")]
    pub async fn my_tool(&self, args: MyArgs) -> Result<CallToolResult, ErrorData> {
        // ...
    }
}
3. Argument Schemas
Derive JsonSchema using the re-exported trait if possible, or ensure schemars version matches rmcp's internal version exactly.

#[derive(serde::Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct MyArgs { ... }

body:
## Goal of the PR
- Add a **PostgreSQL backend for rollback recording** (in addition to SQLite).
- Make rollback backend selection **default to the world’s configured map backend** (`world.mt: backend`) unless explicitly overridden.

## How does the PR work?
- **New backend (guarded by `USE_POSTGRESQL`)**
  - Adds `RollbackManagerPostgreSQL`:
    - `src/server/rollback_postgresql.cpp` (new)
    - `src/server/rollback_postgresql.h` (new)
  - Stores rollback data in PostgreSQL tables (`actor`, `node`, `action`) using prepared statements.
  - Adds indexes intended to speed up common rollback queries (time-window scans and actor-filtered scans).
  - Uses in-process caches to make actor/node ID lookups \(~O(1)\) rather than scanning vectors.
- **Server-side backend selection and logging**
  - When `enable_rollback_recording = true`, the server reads `world.mt`:
    - Use `rollback_backend` if present
    - Else default to `backend` (world map backend)
    - Else default to `sqlite3`
  - For PostgreSQL rollback connections:
    - Prefer `pgsql_rollback_connection`
    - Fall back to `pgsql_connection`
  - Logs which rollback backend is used and **redacts `password=`** in libpq connection strings.
- **Build integration**
  - `src/server/CMakeLists.txt` includes the PostgreSQL rollback backend sources when PostgreSQL support is enabled.
- **Documentation/config updates**
  - Updated:
    - `doc/world_format.md`
    - `doc/lua_api.md`
    - `minetest.conf.example`
    - `builtin/settingtypes.txt`

## Does it resolve any reported issue?
- Not explicitly referenced in this branch.

## Does this relate to a goal in the roadmap?
- Checked `doc/direction.md`: **no explicit mention** of rollback/database backends/PostgreSQL.
- So this PR is **not clearly tied** to a named roadmap item.

## If not a bug fix, why is this PR needed? What usecases does it solve?
- **Servers already using PostgreSQL for map/player/auth data** can keep rollback in the same database system, simplifying operations and backups.
- **Higher write concurrency / operational tooling**: PostgreSQL can be a better fit than SQLite for some multi-admin or high-activity servers.
- **Less configuration drift**: defaulting rollback backend to the world map backend reduces “surprising” split configurations.
- **Safer diagnostics**: logging the selected backend and connection source helps operators, while redacting passwords reduces accidental secret leakage.

## Scope / files changed
- **Added**
  - `src/server/rollback_postgresql.cpp`
  - `src/server/rollback_postgresql.h`
- **Modified**
  - `src/server.cpp`
  - `src/server/CMakeLists.txt`
  - `doc/world_format.md`
  - `doc/lua_api.md`
  - `minetest.conf.example`
  - `builtin/settingtypes.txt`

body:
Segmentation was producing fragments too short to capture real actions, and confusion matrices had insufficient samples due to simple train/test splits. Additionally, amplitude classification was incorrectly using fatigued samples.

## Signal Segmentation Improvements

- **RMS-based detection**: Replace simple thresholding with RMS envelope + Otsu's adaptive thresholding
- **Dual-threshold hysteresis**: High threshold to enter active state, 60% of that to exit—prevents boundary jitter
- **MAV auxiliary envelope**: 70/30 weighted combination with RMS for robust detection
- **Segment refinement**: Min segment length (500ms), merge gap (300ms), boundary extension to local minima

```python
from preprocessing import segment_signal_improved

# New segmentation with configurable parameters
segments = segment_signal_improved(
    signal, fs=2000,
    rms_window_ms=50,
    min_segment_ms=500,
    merge_gap_ms=300,
    use_dual_threshold=True
)
```

## K-Fold Cross-Validation

- Replace `train_test_split` with `StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5)`
- Aggregate predictions across all folds for confusion matrices
- Report mean accuracy ± std across folds

## Amplitude/Fatigue Classification Constraints

- `filter_amplitude_by_fatigue=True` by default—amplitude classes (full/half/invalid) only apply to 'free' fatigue state
- Mirrors existing constraint that fatigue classes only apply to 'full' amplitude

## Tests

Added 8 tests covering envelope computation, adaptive thresholding, and segment merging behavior.

author: rioliu-rh
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a troubleshooting script to help release leads verify operator bundle image availability in registry.stage.redhat.io when stage testing jobs fail.

## Changes

- **New script**: `tools/check_stage_bundle_images.sh`
  - Accepts OCP version as parameter (e.g., 4.19, 4.20)
  - Validates required tools (opm, oc, jq) with installation instructions
  - Extracts bundle images from FBC catalog using `opm render --skip-tls-verify`
  - Checks availability in stage registry using `oc image info`
  - Generates detailed reports and human-readable MISSING_REPORT.txt

- **Slash command integration**: `/ci:analyze-jenkins-failures`
  - Enhanced to automatically run bundle check as Step 1 for stage-testing failures
  - Extracts OCP version from Jenkins job parameters (PULL_SPEC/PAYLOAD_URL)
  - Reports missing bundles separately from test failures
  - No automatic correlation between missing bundles and test failures

- **Bug fix**: Added `--skip-tls-verify` flag to `opm render` command
  - Resolves TLS handshake timeout when pulling FBC catalogs from quay.io
  - Safe for trusted registry sources (quay.io/openshift-art/stage-fbc-fragments)

## Usage

**Standalone**:
```bash
./tools/check_stage_bundle_images.sh 4.20
```

**Via slash command** (automatic):
```bash
/ci:analyze-jenkins-failures https://jenkins-csb-openshift-qe-mastern.dno.corp.redhat.com/job/zstreams/job/Stage-Pipeline/1463/
```

## When to Use

- **Standalone**: Run manually when stage testing job fails to check if missing bundle images are the root cause
- **Slash command**: Automatically invoked during Jenkins stage-testing failure analysis

If bundles are missing, share the MISSING_REPORT.txt with ART team.

## Benefits

- Reduces troubleshooting time for stage testing failures
- Provides actionable data for ART team escalations
- Integrated into AI-assisted failure analysis workflow
- No new dependencies introduced to main codebase
- Self-contained tool with clear error messages
- Handles transient network issues with TLS skip flag

## Related

- Jira: [OCPERT-269](https://issues.redhat.com//browse/OCPERT-269)

- Players who disconnect are now marked as disconnected rather than immediately removed

- If the timer expires, the player is removed and a player_left event is broadcast

author: stephen-shelby
body:
## Why I'm doing:

Default values are used in many critical scenarios in StarRocks, including:
- Fast Schema Evolution: Reading old segments without new columns
- Traditional Schema Change: Rewriting data with `fast_schema_evolution=false`
- Primary Key partial updates: Filling missing columns during partial column inserts
- Column UPSERT mode: Handling partial updates with `partial_update_mode='column'`
- UPDATE DEFAULT: Restoring column values to their defaults

To ensure default values work correctly across all these scenarios and data types, comprehensive test coverage is essential.

## What I'm doing:

Add comprehensive default value test suites for primitive types: **numeric types**, **string types**, **date/datetime types**, and **decimal types** (including Decimal256).

### Test Coverage (Per Type):

Each test suite covers **7 major scenarios**:

1. **Fast Schema Evolution (Test 1)**: 
   - Add columns with defaults to existing table with data
   - Verify old rows fill default values correctly when reading
   - Test mixed old and new data

2. **Traditional Schema Change (Test 2)**: 
   - Add columns with `fast_schema_evolution=false` 
   - Verify defaults are correctly applied during data rewrite

3. **Column UPSERT Mode (Test 3)**:
   - PRIMARY KEY table with `partial_update_mode='column'`
   - Verify partial column inserts fill defaults
   - Test ALTER adding columns in UPSERT mode

4. **Primary Key Partial Update (Test 4)**:
   - Partial column inserts on PRIMARY KEY table
   - Verify defaults fill missing columns
   - Test UPDATE SET column=DEFAULT

5. **Combined Scenarios (Test 5)**:
   - PRIMARY KEY table with ALTER followed by partial inserts
   - Verify old data reads new columns with defaults

6. **Edge Cases (Test 6)**:
   - Numeric: TINYINT, SMALLINT, INT, BIGINT, FLOAT, DOUBLE with max/min/zero/negative values
   - String: VARCHAR, CHAR, STRING with empty/special chars/unicode
   - Date: DATE, DATETIME with various timestamps
   - Decimal: Different precisions (Decimal128: 1-38, **Decimal256: 38-76**)

7. **Different Table Types (Tests 7-8)**:
   - AGGREGATE KEY table with aggregation functions (SUM, MAX, MIN, REPLACE)
   - UNIQUE KEY table

### Test Files Added:
- `test_numeric_default.sql`: TINYINT, SMALLINT, INT, BIGINT, FLOAT, DOUBLE
- `test_string_default.sql`: VARCHAR, CHAR, STRING
- `test_date_default.sql`: DATE, DATETIME
- `test_decimal_default.sql`: DECIMAL (precision 1-76, including Decimal256)

All tests validate that default values are correctly filled in every scenario, ensuring robust default value handling across the entire system.

Fixes #issue

## What type of PR is this:

- [ ] BugFix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Enhancement
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] UT
- [ ] Doc
- [ ] Tool

Does this PR entail a change in behavior?

- [ ] Yes, this PR will result in a change in behavior.
- [x] No, this PR will not result in a change in behavior.

If yes, please specify the type of change:

- [ ] Interface/UI changes: syntax, type conversion, expression evaluation, display information
- [ ] Parameter changes: default values, similar parameters but with different default values
- [ ] Policy changes: use new policy to replace old one, functionality automatically enabled
- [ ] Feature removed
- [ ] Miscellaneous: upgrade & downgrade compatibility, etc.

## Checklist:

- [ ] I have added test cases for my bug fix or my new feature
- [ ] This pr needs user documentation (for new or modified features or behaviors)
  - [ ] I have added documentation for my new feature or new function
- [ ] This is a backport pr

## Bugfix cherry-pick branch check:
- [x] I have checked the version labels which the pr will be auto-backported to the target branch
  - [ ] 4.0
  - [ ] 3.5
  - [ ] 3.4
  - [ ] 3.3

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Adds end-to-end SQL tests verifying default values across table types and update modes (fast schema evolution, traditional schema change, PK partial/column UPSERT), including edge cases and UPDATE DEFAULT.
> 
> - **Tests Added**:
>   - Add `test_numeric_default.sql`, `test_string_default.sql`, `test_date_default.sql`, `test_decimal_default.sql` under `test/sql/test_default_value/T` with expected results in `.../R`.
> - **Coverage**:
>   - Fast Schema Evolution: `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN DEFAULT` on existing data and reads from old segments.
>   - Traditional Schema Change: `fast_schema_evolution=false` with `wait_alter_table_finish()` validations.
>   - Primary Key partial updates: partial inserts into PK tables; Column UPSERT via `SET partial_update_mode='column'` and revert to `auto`.
>   - `UPDATE ... SET col = DEFAULT` behavior on PK tables.
>   - Edge cases across types: boundary numerics/floats, strings (empty/special/unicode), dates/times, and high-precision decimals (including `Decimal(50,15)`/Decimal256).
>   - Different table models: `AGGREGATE KEY` with `SUM/MAX/MIN/REPLACE` defaults and `UNIQUE KEY` tables.

This pull request introduces a major overhaul of the deployment architecture and supporting documentation for the VehEase application. The key changes include migrating the database from MySQL to PostgreSQL, implementing a multi-stage Docker build for optimized frontend and backend handling, updating environment and deployment scripts, and providing comprehensive new documentation for both users and developers. Additionally, the database schema is now fully documented for PostgreSQL.

**Deployment Architecture & Environment Changes:**

- Migrated the database service in `docker-compose.yml` from MySQL to PostgreSQL, updating all relevant environment variables, ports, and volumes for compatibility. The MySQL-specific configuration file `docker/mysql/my.cnf` was removed as it is no longer needed. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e45e45baeda1c1e73482975a664062aa56f20c03dd9d64a827aba57775bed0d3L31-R43) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5dd26b55635090a411ac3609e337c953a33384cbb8ad405a910a7c4d347c4837L1-L5)
- Replaced the monolithic Docker build with a multi-stage Dockerfile: now the frontend is built with Node.js and Vite, PHP dependencies are installed in a separate Composer stage, and the final image uses PHP 8.4 FPM with assets and vendor files copied from the build stages. PHP is now configured with PostgreSQL support (`pdo_pgsql`) instead of MySQL.

**Documentation & Developer Experience:**

- Replaced the generic Laravel `README.md` with a detailed project-specific version, including live deployment info, demo credentials, tech stack, and a summary of completed and planned features.
- Removed the old deployment guide (`DEPLOYMENT.md`) and the deployment shell script (`deploy.sh`) in favor of a simplified and updated Docker-based workflow. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-04615394c116398fb5fcb0aa2d880df854202e4c94907dc81cd2647101ad3306L1-L292) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-30883d1df2fc62f59d66255a70dc05f60d3d4ef4d3957e6e3e38e62f6e471bd0L1-L63)

**Database Schema:**

- Added a comprehensive PostgreSQL schema and type definitions in `docs/Vehease_2025-12-17T04_41_58.856Z.sql`, covering all tables, enums, and relationships required for the application.

---

**Most important changes:**

**1. Deployment & Infrastructure Modernization**
- Migrated database from MySQL to PostgreSQL in `docker-compose.yml` and dropped MySQL configuration files. Updated all environment variables and ports to match PostgreSQL conventions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e45e45baeda1c1e73482975a664062aa56f20c03dd9d64a827aba57775bed0d3L31-R43) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-5dd26b55635090a411ac3609e337c953a33384cbb8ad405a910a7c4d347c4837L1-L5)
- Introduced a multi-stage Docker build: frontend assets built with Node.js/Vite, PHP dependencies installed via Composer, and final image optimized for production with PHP 8.4 FPM and PostgreSQL support.

**2. Documentation & Developer Experience**
- Rewrote `README.md` to provide project-specific details: live demo, login credentials, tech stack, and development roadmap, improving onboarding and transparency for contributors and users.
- Removed outdated deployment instructions and scripts (`DEPLOYMENT.md`, `deploy.sh`) to avoid confusion and reflect the new Docker-based workflow. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-04615394c116398fb5fcb0aa2d880df854202e4c94907dc81cd2647101ad3306L1-L292) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-30883d1df2fc62f59d66255a70dc05f60d3d4ef4d3957e6e3e38e62f6e471bd0L1-L63)

**3. Database Schema Documentation**
- Added a new, detailed PostgreSQL schema (`docs/Vehease_2025-12-17T04_41_58.856Z.sql`) with all necessary enums, tables, and foreign key relationships, ensuring clarity for backend development and migrations.

author: sagaskoyer
body:
## Summary

Implements a complete Python CLI tool that batch-converts video files to audio format (.m4a) with advanced processing options.

## Features Implemented

✅ **Core Functionality**
- Batch process all video files in a directory
- Convert to .m4a (AAC audio, 160kbps)
- Support for 15+ video formats (.mp4, .mov, .avi, .mkv, .webm, etc.)
- Output to same directory with same filename

✅ **User Options**
- Remove silence: Remove audio below -55dB lasting >1.2 seconds (throughout entire audio)
- Normalize audio: Normalize to -16 LUFS for comfortable listening
- Track selection: Choose which audio track to extract (1, 2, 3, etc.)
- Normalization is always applied AFTER silence removal when both are selected

✅ **Error Handling**
- Continues processing all files even if some fail
- Displays detailed error summary at the end
- Overwrites existing .m4a files as specified

✅ **Packaging**
- Standalone Windows .exe with bundled Python + FFmpeg (~100-150MB)
- No dependencies required for end users
- PyInstaller configuration included

## Project Structure

```
video_to_audio/
├── __init__.py          # Package initialization
├── __main__.py          # Entry point (python -m video_to_audio)
├── cli.py               # Main CLI orchestration and user interaction
├── converter.py         # Multi-step conversion pipeline
├── ffmpeg_commands.py   # FFmpeg command construction
├── file_utils.py        # File discovery and validation
├── prompts.py           # Interactive user prompts
└── config.py            # Configuration constants
```

## Testing

All features tested on Linux:
- ✅ Basic conversion
- ✅ Silence removal only
- ✅ Normalization only
- ✅ Both silence removal + normalization
- ✅ Multi-step processing pipeline with temp files
- ✅ Error handling and cleanup

## Documentation

- **README.md**: Comprehensive user guide with usage examples
- **BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md**: Detailed build guide for Windows/macOS/Linux
- **video_to_audio.spec**: PyInstaller configuration with comments

## How to Build Windows Executable

1. On Windows machine with Python installed
2. Download FFmpeg binary to `ffmpeg/windows/ffmpeg.exe`
3. Install PyInstaller: `pip install pyinstaller`
4. Build: `pyinstaller video_to_audio.spec`
5. Find executable at `dist/video-to-audio.exe`

See BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md for detailed steps.

## Example Usage

```
video-to-audio.exe

Enter directory path: C:\Users\Name\Videos
Directory: C:\Users\Name\Videos

Configuration Options:
Remove stretches of silence? (y/n): y
Normalize audio levels for listening? (y/n): y
Audio track to use (1/2/3): 1

Found 5 video file(s)

[1/5] Converting: lecture.mp4
      Output: lecture.m4a
      Status: ✓ Completed

...

All files converted successfully!
```

## Technical Details

**Processing Pipeline (when both options selected):**
1. Extract audio: `video.mp4` → `temp1.m4a` (with track selection)
2. Remove silence: `temp1.m4a` → `temp2.m4a`
3. Normalize: `temp2.m4a` → `video.m4a`
4. Cleanup temp files

**FFmpeg Commands:**
- Base: `ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -vn -c:a aac -b:a 160k -map 0:a:0 -y output.m4a`
- Silence: `ffmpeg -i input.m4a -af silenceremove=... -c:a aac -y output.m4a`
- Normalize: `ffmpeg -i input.m4a -af loudnorm=I=-16:... -c:a aac -y output.m4a`

## Next Steps

To create the Windows .exe for distribution:
1. Build on Windows machine following BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md
2. Test the .exe on a clean Windows system
3. Create a GitHub release with the executable attached

body:
Heudiconv caches DICOM file paths in `.heudiconv/<subject>/info/filegroup.json` and reloads them when `edit.txt` exists. When users manually reorganize DICOM directories between runs, cached paths become stale, causing `TraitError: file does not exist` failures.

## Changes

**Validate DICOM files before processing**
- Search with multiple patterns (`*.dcm`, `*.DCM`, `*.dicom`, `*.DICOM`) for Python 3.9+ compatibility
- Raise descriptive error if no files found after extraction
- Log directory structure and file counts for debugging

**Clear stale cache**
- Remove `.heudiconv/<subject>/` directory before running conversion
- Forces heudiconv to discover actual directory structure instead of using cached paths

```python
# Validate extraction succeeded
dicom_patterns = ["**/*.dcm", "**/*.DCM", "**/*.dicom", "**/*.DICOM"]
dicom_files = []
for pattern in dicom_patterns:
    dicom_files.extend(dicom_extract_dir.glob(pattern))

if not dicom_files:
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"No DICOM files found in {dicom_extract_dir}")

# Clear cache to avoid stale paths
heudiconv_cache = bids_dir / ".heudiconv" / args.subid
if heudiconv_cache.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(heudiconv_cache)
```

This ensures manually curated directories process correctly without requiring users to manually clear caches.

author: copilot
body:
Users see "System is initializing. Please wait a moment and refresh the page" when visiting `/admin/login` before database connects. The async initialization pattern starts the server immediately but offers no visibility into connection state or automatic recovery.

## Changes

### Retry mechanism with exponential backoff
- `connectDBWithRetry()` attempts connection 5 times: 2s → 4s → 8s → 16s → 30s (capped)
- Thread-safe `InitStatus` struct tracks ready state, DB status, last error, retry count

### New endpoints
- `/ready` - Returns 503 until fully initialized (for K8s/Cloud Run readiness probes)
- `/admin/status` - JSON status for AJAX polling

### Login page auto-refresh
- JavaScript polls `/admin/status` and auto-reloads when ready
- Form inputs disabled during initialization with live status updates

### Database connection optimization
- Added `connect_timeout=10` for faster failure detection
- Increased pool: 5 idle → 10 open, 15min lifetime, 5min idle timeout

```go
// Retry with exponential backoff
func connectDBWithRetry(maxRetries int, initialDelay time.Duration) *gorm.DB {
    delay := initialDelay
    for attempt := 1; attempt <= maxRetries; attempt++ {
        db, err := config.InitDB()
        if err == nil {
            return db
        }
        if attempt < maxRetries {
            time.Sleep(delay)
            delay = min(delay*2, maxDelayBetweenRetries)
        }
    }
    return nil
}
```

author: arpamuji
body:
This pull request introduces major changes to the VehEase project, focusing on migrating the backend database from MySQL to PostgreSQL, updating the Docker-based deployment and build process, and improving project documentation. It also removes legacy deployment scripts and documentation that are no longer relevant after these changes. The most important changes are grouped below:

**Database Migration and Schema Updates:**

* Migrated the backend database from MySQL to PostgreSQL, updating the `docker-compose.yml` service for `db` to use the `postgres:16-alpine` image, and adjusting environment variables and ports accordingly.
* Added a new SQL schema file (`docs/Vehease_2025-12-17T04_41_58.856Z.sql`) defining all tables, enum types, and relationships for PostgreSQL, reflecting the new database structure.
* Removed the MySQL configuration file `docker/mysql/my.cnf` as it is no longer needed.

**Docker and Build Process Improvements:**

* Rewrote the `Dockerfile` to use a multi-stage build: first building frontend assets with Node.js, then installing PHP dependencies with Composer, and finally assembling the application in a PHP 8.4 FPM container. The new Dockerfile is optimized for PostgreSQL and removes previous Node.js/Bun steps.

**Deployment and Documentation Cleanup:**

* Removed the `DEPLOYMENT.md` file, which contained outdated deployment instructions for the previous architecture.
* Deleted the `deploy.sh` deployment script, as the deployment process has been significantly changed and streamlined.

**Project Documentation Improvements:**

* Overhauled the `README.md` to provide a clear project overview, live deployment link, feature status, demo credentials, tech stack, and database documentation location, making it more user-friendly and informative.

These changes collectively modernize the infrastructure, simplify deployment, and improve maintainability and onboarding for new developers.

body:
## GitHub Actions Workflow Implementation - ✅ COMPLETED

- [x] Create `.github/workflows/tools-deploy.yml` with infrastructure, build, and deploy jobs
- [x] Configure workflow to trigger on `develop`, `integration/**`, and `master` branches
- [x] Set up automated CloudFormation stack deployment for ECR, Lambda, and CloudFront
- [x] Set up build job with ECR login and Docker image push
- [x] Set up deploy job with Lambda function update
- [x] Add health check verification step with robust error handling

- [x] Run code review and address all feedback

- [x] Verify all requirements from issue #104 are met
- [x] Organize documentation in Tools-specific scope
- [x] Simplify to single-region architecture (us-east-1)
- [x] Align authentication with existing infrastructure workflows (access keys)
- [x] Implement full automation with automatic CloudFormation deployment
- [x] Integrate CloudFront deployment with automatic certificate and domain discovery
- [x] **Update development domain naming convention to `dev-tools.example.com`**

## 📁 Documentation Structure

Documentation has been organized to properly scope the Tools app deployment guide:

### Updated
- **`docs/services/tools/deployment.md`** - Complete Tools app deployment and operations guide
  - **Simplified single-region architecture**: All resources in `us-east-1`
  - **Fully automated CI/CD**: CloudFormation stacks for ECR, Lambda, and CloudFront deployed automatically
  - Manual deployment steps (Docker build, ECR push, Lambda update)
  - **GitHub Actions CI/CD using existing IAM user**: Consistent with infrastructure workflows
  - **CloudFront integration**: Automatic deployment with certificate and domain from shared infrastructure
  - **Updated domain naming**: `dev-tools.example.com` for development environment
  - Workflow details and troubleshooting
  - Monitoring, operations, and incident response procedures

- **`.github/workflows/tools-deploy.yml`** - Fully automated deployment workflow with CloudFormation

## Complete Automation - Infrastructure as Code

The workflow achieves **full automation** by automatically deploying all required CloudFormation stacks, including CloudFront:

### Workflow Structure

1. **Infrastructure Job**: Deploys ECR CloudFormation stack
2. **Build Job**: Queries ECR stack, builds and pushes Docker image
3. **Deploy Job**: 
   - Deploys Lambda CloudFormation stack with new image
   - Verifies Lambda deployment with health check
   - **Deploys CloudFront CloudFormation stack** with automatic certificate and domain discovery
   - Displays CloudFront distribution information

### CloudFront Integration

The workflow **automatically discovers** ACM certificate and domain configuration from the shared infrastructure:

**Certificate Discovery:**
- Queries CloudFormation export `nagiyu-shared-acm-certificate-arn`
- No manual certificate ARN configuration needed

**Domain Discovery:**
- Queries CloudFormation export `nagiyu-shared-acm-domain-name` for base domain
- Automatically constructs subdomain based on environment:
  - **Production** (`master` branch): `tools.example.com`
  - **Development** (`develop`, `integration/**`): `dev-tools.example.com`

### Key Features

- **Zero Manual Setup**: No need to pre-create CloudFormation stacks or configure certificates
- **Idempotent Operations**: Uses `--no-fail-on-empty-changeset` - only applies changes when needed
- **Single Source of Truth**: CloudFormation templates in repository define all infrastructure
- **Fully Automated**: Push to branch → entire infrastructure (ECR + Lambda + CloudFront) + application deployed automatically
- **Dynamic Resource Discovery**: All resource names, certificates, and domains come from CloudFormation
- **Shared Infrastructure Integration**: Leverages existing ACM stack exports
- **Consistent Naming**: Development domains follow `{env}-{service}` pattern (e.g., `dev-tools`, `staging-tools`)

### Benefits

1. **True Infrastructure as Code**: CloudFormation templates are deployed automatically on every workflow run
2. **No Manual Prerequisites**: Everything from infrastructure to CDN deployment is automated
3. **Reproducible**: Can recreate entire environment from scratch by running the workflow
4. **Safe Updates**: CloudFormation only applies changes when templates or parameters change
5. **No Coordination Needed**: Don't need to manually create or update stacks before deployment
6. **Shared Infrastructure Leverage**: Reuses ACM certificate and domain configuration without duplication

## Authentication Method - Access Keys

The Tools deployment uses the **same authentication method** as existing infrastructure workflows for consistency:

### Existing IAM Setup (Reused)
- **IAM User**: `nagiyu-github-actions` (defined in `infra/shared/iam/users/github-actions-user.yaml`)
- **Policies Attached**:
  - `nagiyu-deploy-policy-core`
  - `nagiyu-deploy-policy-container` (includes ECR permissions)
  - `nagiyu-deploy-policy-application` (includes Lambda permissions)
  - `nagiyu-deploy-policy-integration`

### GitHub Secrets (Already Configured)
- `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` - Shared with ACM, VPC workflows
- `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` - Shared with ACM, VPC workflows
- `AWS_REGION` - Set to `us-east-1`

**No additional secrets needed for CloudFront** - certificate and domain are discovered automatically from CloudFormation exports.

### Benefits of This Approach
1. **Consistency**: Same authentication method as existing infrastructure workflows (ACM, VPC)
2. **No Additional Setup**: Uses already-configured IAM user and GitHub secrets
3. **Shared Permissions**: IAM policies already include necessary ECR, Lambda, CloudFront, and CloudFormation permissions
4. **Simpler Onboarding**: No need to set up OIDC provider or additional IAM roles

## Simplified Single-Region Architecture

All resources are deployed to `us-east-1` for operational simplicity:

| Resource | Region | Reason |
|----------|--------|--------|
| **ECR** | `us-east-1` | Unified with other resources |
| **Lambda** | `us-east-1` | Same region as ECR and CloudFront |
| **CloudFront** | Global service | CloudFormation stack in `us-east-1` |
| **ACM Certificate** | `us-east-1` | Required for CloudFront |
| **IAM** | Global service | Managed via `us-east-1` |

### Benefits of Single-Region Approach

1. **Simplified Management**: All resources in one region
2. **No Cross-Region Complexity**: Avoids CloudFormation export/import issues
3. **ACM Integration**: Natural fit with CloudFront ACM requirements
4. **Easier Troubleshooting**: All logs and resources in one console view
5. **Lower Deployment Overhead**: Single region to deploy and manage

For a tools app with infrequent deployment, operational simplicity outweighs the marginal latency difference. CloudFront still provides global edge caching for static assets.

## Scope

The GitHub Actions workflow and its documentation are Tools-specific:
- Uses shared IAM user with permissions scoped appropriately via managed policies
- Workflow triggers on `services/tools/**` and `infra/tools/**` path changes
- All deployment procedures are for the Tools application
- Automatically deploys and manages Tools-specific CloudFormation stacks (ECR, Lambda, CloudFront)
- Integrates with shared infrastructure (ACM) via CloudFormation exports

Therefore, documentation is properly placed in `docs/services/tools/deployment.md` following the repository's service-scoped documentation pattern.

author: yellow-shine
body:
This pull request introduces support for dynamic compute unit (CU) autoscaling for clusters, allowing users to configure minimum and maximum CUs for autoscaling via the new `cu_settings` attribute. It also ensures that `cu_settings` and `cu_size` cannot be set simultaneously, updates the resource schema and validation logic, and adds comprehensive test coverage for these features.

Key changes include:

**Dynamic Autoscaling Feature:**

* Added new `cu_settings` attribute (with nested `dynamic_scaling` for `min` and `max` CUs) to the cluster resource schema, including documentation and validation to prevent configuration conflicts with `cu_size`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-10b1fe1d02136e4a796a1cff0f979142ef11ae2764f4ecde0fa565309da66160R56-R63) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-10b1fe1d02136e4a796a1cff0f979142ef11ae2764f4ecde0fa565309da66160R218-R243) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-10b1fe1d02136e4a796a1cff0f979142ef11ae2764f4ecde0fa565309da66160L95) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-ea87985827a5e33692d9699416d9144971b191e9688a542125e8f31b5133adbdR74) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-ea87985827a5e33692d9699416d9144971b191e9688a542125e8f31b5133adbdR97-R113)
* Implemented backend support for modifying and retrieving autoscaling settings, including new parameter types, API client methods, and store logic for handling autoscaling updates and state population. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a8bb1ddff646d3a8d525c3a8d951dd1c8e1037f8655f7a8d25be2764c0625493R83-R101) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a8bb1ddff646d3a8d525c3a8d951dd1c8e1037f8655f7a8d25be2764c0625493R186-R196) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-578da58b211e381313acfa188951de2bbf2161c3d361563224367f1c8ffefcc1R25) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-578da58b211e381313acfa188951de2bbf2161c3d361563224367f1c8ffefcc1R40-R47) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-578da58b211e381313acfa188951de2bbf2161c3d361563224367f1c8ffefcc1R83-R85) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-578da58b211e381313acfa188951de2bbf2161c3d361563224367f1c8ffefcc1L115-R132)

**Validation and State Management:**

* Enforced mutual exclusivity between `cu_size` and `cu_settings` at the schema and configuration validation level, and added logic to handle updates and validation for autoscaling settings. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-10b1fe1d02136e4a796a1cff0f979142ef11ae2764f4ecde0fa565309da66160R56-R63) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-10b1fe1d02136e4a796a1cff0f979142ef11ae2764f4ecde0fa565309da66160R571-R607) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-10b1fe1d02136e4a796a1cff0f979142ef11ae2764f4ecde0fa565309da66160L567-R641) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-26f09143a3b353cb8cf3f3cebc2fd1d2f91a129447bc4c847539d1f3f7937f50R192-R195)
* Updated the cluster resource model to support new autoscaling fields and equality checks for change detection. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-26f09143a3b353cb8cf3f3cebc2fd1d2f91a129447bc4c847539d1f3f7937f50R17-R49) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-26f09143a3b353cb8cf3f3cebc2fd1d2f91a129447bc4c847539d1f3f7937f50R70-R77)

**Testing:**

* Added acceptance tests for the new `cu_settings` feature, including tests for conflict validation and updating autoscaling parameters. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f7ed30a5856dd3b3074683accc67b4cc8d59b274232dfc67bf35b33fb7e2a8a5R20) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f7ed30a5856dd3b3074683accc67b4cc8d59b274232dfc67bf35b33fb7e2a8a5R351-R457)

**Other Improvements:**

* Minor test and import improvements to ensure robust error handling and validation in project tests. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a715edf0b940ddcfb102fdc2d20338de81666970c26e566474841ff507c78573R71) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a715edf0b940ddcfb102fdc2d20338de81666970c26e566474841ff507c78573R96)
* Updated imports and removed unused default for `cu_size` to align with new autoscaling logic. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-10b1fe1d02136e4a796a1cff0f979142ef11ae2764f4ecde0fa565309da66160R11) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-10b1fe1d02136e4a796a1cff0f979142ef11ae2764f4ecde0fa565309da66160R20-R21) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-10b1fe1d02136e4a796a1cff0f979142ef11ae2764f4ecde0fa565309da66160L95)

These changes collectively provide a robust foundation for dynamic cluster scaling and improve the flexibility and reliability of cluster resource management.

author: progami
body:
## Summary
Apply the same POSTED order filter to inventory balance endpoints:
- `/api/inventory/balances` - main inventory page
- `/api/inventory/ledger-based` - ledger-based inventory view

## Problem
The previous fix only updated `/api/transactions/ledger`, but the main inventory page uses `/api/inventory/balances` which wasn't filtering by PO status.

## Solution
Added the same filter to both inventory endpoints:
```typescript
OR: [
  { purchaseOrderId: null },
  { purchaseOrder: { status: 'POSTED' } }
]
```

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify orders in REVIEW don't appear in inventory balances
- [ ] Verify orders in POSTED appear correctly
- [ ] Verify transactions without PO links still appear

author: vinceyyy
body:
## Summary

This PR addresses stability issues where the app stops working after running in ECS for a period, including login failures and debugger statements appearing in production. It implements a three-phase improvement plan covering security, architecture simplification, and infrastructure enhancements.

**Key Changes:**
- Upgrade Next.js 15 → 16 to address security vulnerabilities
- Replace Server-Sent Events (SSE) with simple 1-second polling for simpler debugging
- Improve authentication with cryptographically signed session tokens
- Optimize scheduler to reduce DynamoDB calls
- Add production-ready logging and infrastructure configuration

---

## Architecture Changes

### Before: SSE-Based Real-Time Updates

```
┌─────────────┐     SSE Connection      ┌─────────────┐
│   Browser   │◄──────────────────────►│   Server    │
│             │    /api/events          │             │
│  useSSE()   │    (persistent)         │  EventSource│
│             │                         │             │
│             │◄─── operation_update ───│  emit()     │
│             │◄─── scheduler_event ────│             │
│             │◄─── heartbeat (30s) ────│             │
└─────────────┘                         └─────────────┘
                                              │
                                              ▼
                                        ┌───────────┐
                                        │ DynamoDB  │
                                        └───────────┘

Problems:
- Persistent connections hard to debug
- Connection drops cause stale UI
- SSE endpoint complexity
- Memory overhead from event listeners
```

### After: Simple Polling (1-second interval)

```
┌─────────────┐      HTTP Requests      ┌─────────────┐
│   Browser   │─────────────────────────│   Server    │
│             │    /api/operations      │             │
│ usePolling()│    ?activeOnly=true     │             │
│             │    (stateless)          │             │
│             │                         │             │
│             │──► Poll every 1s ──────►│  GSI Query  │
│             │                         │             │
└─────────────┘                         └─────────────┘
                                              │
                                              ▼
                                        ┌───────────┐
                                        │ DynamoDB  │
                                        │   (GSI)   │
                                        └───────────┘

Benefits:
- Stateless, easy to debug
- Automatic retry on failures
- Instant updates (1s latency)
- No persistent connections
- Efficient GSI queries (~$0.16/month per user)
```

---

## Authentication Flow Change

### Before: Plain Cookie Value

```
┌──────────┐    passcode     ┌──────────┐
│  Login   │────────────────►│  Server  │
│   Page   │                 │          │
│          │◄────────────────│          │
│          │  Set-Cookie:    │          │
│          │  auth-token=    │          │
│          │  "authenticated"│          │
└──────────┘                 └──────────┘

Problems:
- Cookie value is predictable
- No expiry validation
- Vulnerable to cookie injection
- Cookie maxAge was wrong (1000 days!)
```

### After: HMAC-Signed Tokens

```
┌──────────┐    passcode     ┌──────────┐
│  Login   │────────────────►│  Server  │
│   Page   │                 │          │
│          │                 │ 1. Validate passcode
│          │                 │    (constant-time)
│          │                 │ 2. Create token:
│          │                 │    {expiry}.{signature}
│          │◄────────────────│ 3. HMAC-SHA256 sign
│          │  Set-Cookie:    │          │
│          │  auth-token=    │          │
│          │  {expiry}.{sig} │          │
│          │  maxAge=24h     │          │
└──────────┘                 └──────────┘

Security improvements:
- Cryptographically signed tokens
- Embedded expiry timestamp
- Constant-time comparison (timing attack protection)
- Correct 24-hour maxAge (was 1000 days!)
```

---

## Scheduler Optimization

### Before: Separate Queries

```
processScheduledOperations()
    └── Query GSI: status = 'scheduled'

processAutoDestroy()
    └── Query GSI: status IN ('running', 'completed')

processExpiredTakeHomes()           ──┐
    └── Scan: type='takehome'         │ Duplicate!
                                      │
processActivatedTakeHomesAutoDestroy()│
    └── Scan: type='takehome'       ──┘
```

### After: Combined Queries

```
processScheduledOperations()
    └── Query GSI: status = 'scheduled'

processAutoDestroy()
    └── Query GSI: status IN ('running', 'completed')

processTakeHomes()                  ── Single query!
    └── Scan: type='takehome'
        ├── Check expiry
        └── Check auto-destroy
```

---

## Logging Format Change

### Before: Plain Text

```
2024-01-15T10:30:00Z [INFO] [auth] Login successful
```

### After: JSON (CloudWatch Logs Insights)

```json
{
  "timestamp": "2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z",
  "level": "info",
  "service": "portal",
  "component": "auth",
  "message": "Login successful",
  "requestId": "abc123",
  "clientIp": "192.168.1.1"
}
```

Enables CloudWatch Logs Insights queries:
```sql
fields @timestamp, level, component, message
| filter level = "error"
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 100
```

---

## File Changes Summary

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/proxy.ts` | New - Next.js 16 proxy (replaces middleware) |
| `src/lib/auth.ts` | New - HMAC token creation/validation |
| `src/hooks/usePolling.ts` | New - Simple 1-second polling hook |
| `src/lib/logger.ts` | Enhanced - JSON output, redaction, requestId |
| `src/lib/scheduler.ts` | Optimized - Combined take-home queries |
| `src/app/api/auth/login/route.ts` | Fixed - Correct maxAge, secure tokens |
| `src/middleware.ts` | Deleted - Replaced by proxy.ts |
| `src/hooks/useSSE.ts` | Deleted - Replaced by polling |
| `src/app/api/events/route.ts` | Deleted - SSE endpoint removed |
| `infra/modules/compute/*` | Enhanced - Configurable sizing |
| `infra/environments/prod/main.tf` | Updated - 1 vCPU, 2GB RAM |

---

## Testing

### Automated Testing (Completed)
- [x] TypeScript compilation passes
- [x] Build succeeds without errors
- [x] ESLint passes with no warnings
- [x] Unit tests pass
- [x] No secret leaks detected (gitleaks)

### Manual Testing (TODO)
- [x] Login with correct passcode → success, redirected to dashboard
- [x] Login with wrong passcode → 401 error, stays on login page
- [x] Session expires after 24 hours → redirected to login
- [x] Create interview → status updates every 1 second
- [x] Destroy interview → status updates every 1 second
- [ ] Schedule interview → shows scheduled state, provisions on time
- [ ] Auto-destroy fires at configured time
- [ ] CloudWatch logs show JSON format with proper fields
- [ ] No debugger statements in production DevTools

---

author: copilot
body:
Migrates API tokens, webhooks, and OAuth connections from client-side stubs (localStorage/Spark KV) to D1-backed REST APIs with proper cryptographic security.

## Changes

### API Tokens
- Generate tokens as `dcv_live_<32-hex>`, hash with SHA-256 before storage
- Endpoints: `POST/GET/DELETE /api/tokens` (admin/owner only)
- Token revealed once on creation, never retrievable afterward
- Frontend switched from localStorage to real API calls

### Webhooks
- Migration `0007_webhooks.sql` adds webhook_endpoints table
- CRUD endpoints: `POST/GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/webhooks` (admin/owner only)
- Payloads signed with HMAC-SHA256, signature in `X-DCVaaS-Signature` header
- Consumer worker dispatches `domain.active` and `domain.error` events on status changes
- Frontend WebhooksPage now persists to D1 instead of Spark KV

### OAuth Connections
- Endpoints: `POST /api/oauth/exchange`, `GET/DELETE /api/oauth/connections`
- Access/refresh tokens encrypted with AES-GCM using PBKDF2-derived keys (100k iterations)
- Requires `OAUTH_ENCRYPTION_KEY` environment variable (fails securely if unset)
- Provider-specific code exchange stubs ready for implementation

### Sync Loop
- Cron now queries active domains not updated in 24+ hours to refresh expiration dates
- Consumer extracts `expires_at` from Cloudflare SSL data when available

## Example

```bash
# Create token (returns plaintext once)
curl -X POST /api/tokens \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <existing-token>" \
  -d '{"name": "CI Token"}'

# Use token for API calls
curl /api/domains \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer dcv_live_abc123..."
```

```javascript
// Verify webhook signature
const hmac = crypto
  .createHmac('sha256', webhook_secret)
  .update(JSON.stringify(payload))
  .digest('hex');
  
if (hmac === req.headers['x-dcvaas-signature']) {
  // Process webhook
}
```

## Deployment

1. Set `OAUTH_ENCRYPTION_KEY` via `wrangler secret put`
2. Apply migration: `wrangler d1 execute dcvaas-db --remote --file=workers/api/migrations/0007_webhooks.sql`
3. Deploy api, consumer, and cron workers

See `PRODUCTION_HARDENING_SUMMARY.md` for complete deployment checklist and API documentation.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> 
> ----
> 
> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>Finalize Production Hardening: Backend Implementation for Tokens, Webhooks & OAuth</issue_title>
> <issue_description>Context
> The application core (Teams, Billing, Branding, Domain CRUD) is complete. However, several "Developer Platform" features currently rely on client-side stubs (localStorage or Spark KV) and need to be moved to the real Cloudflare D1 backend to be production-ready.
> 
> Objectives
> Migrate API Tokens to Backend: Move token creation from localStorage to D1.
> 
> Implement Webhook System: Move webhook config from spark.kv to D1 and build the dispatcher.
> 
> Implement OAuth Backend: Build the route to handle OAuth code exchange for the "Single Click" feature.
> 
> Upgrade Sync Loop: Ensure active domains are polled for expiration updates.
> 
> Task 1: API Token Backend Implementation
> The api_tokens table already exists in schema.sql.
> 
> Backend (workers/api):
> 
> Create POST /api/tokens: Generate a secure random token, hash it (SHA-256), and store the hash in D1. Return the plaintext once.
> 
> Create GET /api/tokens: Return list of tokens (masked) for the org.
> 
> Create DELETE /api/tokens/:id: Revoke a token.
> 
> Frontend:
> 
> Update src/lib/data.ts to call these real endpoints instead of using localStorage.
> 
> Task 2: Outbound Webhook System
> The WebhooksPage.tsx currently saves to spark.kv.
> 
> Database:
> 
> Create a migration for a webhook_endpoints table (id, org_id, url, secret, events, created_at).
> 
> Backend (workers/api):
> 
> Create CRUD endpoints (POST/GET/DELETE) for webhooks at /api/webhooks.
> 
> Implement a dispatchWebhook(orgId, event, payload) utility.
> 
> This utility should:
> 
> Fetch enabled endpoints for the org.
> 
> Sign the payload using HMAC-SHA256 and the stored secret.
> 
> POST the payload to the user's URL with X-DCVaaS-Signature.
> 
> Integration:
> 
> Call dispatchWebhook in handlers/sync-status.ts when a domain becomes active.
> 
> Task 3: OAuth "Single Click" Backend
> The oauth_connections table exists, but is unused.
> 
> Backend (workers/api):
> 
> Create POST /api/oauth/exchange:
> 
> Accepts { provider, code, redirectUri }.
> 
> Exchanges code with provider (e.g., Cloudflare/GoDaddy) for access/refresh tokens.
> 
> Encrypts tokens using AES-GCM (utilize existing crypto.ts helpers).
> 
> Stores encrypted blobs in oauth_connections.
> 
> Frontend:
> 
> Update SettingsPage.tsx to add a "Connect DNS Provider" button that initiates this flow.
> 
> Task 4: Sync Loop for Active Domains
> Currently, workers/cron/src/index.ts only queries domains where status != 'active'.
> 
> Update Cron Logic:
> 
> Modify query to also include active domains that haven't been updated in > 24 hours:
> 
> SQL
> 
> SELECT * FROM domains 
> WHERE status != 'active' 
>    OR (status = 'active' AND updated_at < datetime('now', '-1 day'))
> LIMIT ?
> This ensures the dashboard reflects the true expires_at date as Cloudflare auto-renews the certificate in the background.
> 
> Acceptance Criteria
> [ ] Creating an API token persists to D1 and works for curl requests.
> 
> [ ] Webhook configuration persists to D1, and test events are received at the target URL.
>

author: cfsmp3
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a critical double-free bug that caused CCExtractor to crash with exit code 134 (SIGABRT) when processing teletext streams. The crash occurred during cleanup after processing completed.

## Problem

The teletext context (`TeletextCtx`) pointer was shared between two structures:
- `dec_ctx->private_data` (decoder context)
- `cinfo->codec_private_data` (capture info in `cinfo_tree`)

**Crash sequence:**
1. `general_loop()` calls `telxcc_close(&dec_ctx->private_data)` → frees TeletextCtx, NULLs `dec_ctx->private_data`
2. But `cinfo->codec_private_data` still points to the freed memory (not NULLed!)
3. During cleanup, `dinit_cap()` sees non-NULL `cinfo->codec_private_data`
4. `dinit_cap()` calls `telxcc_close()` again → **double-free crash**

## Root Cause

This bug was exposed by commit 7e1a01447 ("fix(ocr): Improve DVB subtitle OCR quality") which added cleanup code to `dinit_cap()` to free `codec_private_data`. The `telxcc_close()` call in `general_loop()` has existed since 2015, but the double-free only became possible after the new cleanup code was added.

## Solution

After `telxcc_close()` frees the teletext context in `general_loop()`, iterate through all `cinfo` entries and NULL out any that shared the same pointer:

```c
if (dec_ctx->codec == CCX_CODEC_TELETEXT)
{
    void *saved_private_data = dec_ctx->private_data;
    telxcc_close(&dec_ctx->private_data, &dec_ctx->dec_sub);
    // NULL out any cinfo entries that shared this private_data pointer
    if (saved_private_data && ctx->demux_ctx)
    {
        struct cap_info *cinfo_iter;
        list_for_each_entry(cinfo_iter, &ctx->demux_ctx->cinfo_tree.all_stream, ...)
        {
            if (cinfo_iter->codec_private_data == saved_private_data)
                cinfo_iter->codec_private_data = NULL;
        }
    }
}
```
